draft.title: Homemade Incubated Yogurt

steps.text: Heat the milk in a pot until it just steams, taking care not to let it boil.

why.text: Heat milk until steaming without boiling.
why.quote: make sure it doesn't boil uh just until it steams a little bit

why.text: Heating denatures whey proteins, which allows the yogurt to set into a firm gel.

steps.text: Stir 1/3 cup of sugar into the heated milk until blended.
Mix the plain yogurt starter into the milk mixture until well combined.
Pour the mixture into small jars.
Place all the jars into the incubator and let sit for 8 to 12 hours.
Chill the jars in the refrigerator (or freezer) before serving.

notes: Retained order from transcript, but flagged missing step: heated milk must cool before adding live cultures.

questions.question: Should the milk cool down before stirring in the yogurt starter?
questions.why_it_matters: Stirring live yogurt cultures into steaming hot milk will kill the beneficial bacteria and prevent the yogurt from setting.
questions.suggestion: Cool the milk to about 110°F (43°C) before mixing in the yogurt starter.

questions.question: What size yogurt container did you mean by '10 in'?
questions.why_it_matters: Using the wrong ratio of yogurt starter to milk affects fermentation time and final texture.
questions.suggestion: Use a 6 oz container of plain unflavored yogurt.

questions.question: What type of incubator is used, and what temperature should it be set to?
questions.why_it_matters: Yogurt requires a stable temperature around 105°F to 112°F to ferment safely without killing the cultures or allowing bad bacteria to grow.
questions.suggestion: Use an electric yogurt maker or a warm oven held at 110°F (43°C).

final.title: Homemade Incubated Yogurt

ingredients.note: Transcript misheard 'small single cup' as '10 in'

steps.text: Heat the milk in a pot until it just steams, taking care not to let it boil.

why.text: Heat milk until steaming without boiling.
why.quote: make sure it doesn't boil uh just until it steams a little bit

why.text: Heating denatures whey proteins, allowing the yogurt to set into a firm gel.

steps.text: Stir 1/3 cup of sugar into the heated milk until dissolved.
Allow the heated milk mixture to cool down before adding the yogurt starter.

why.text: The milk needs to cool before adding the starter.
Adding starter to boiling or very hot milk kills the active live bacterial cultures.

steps.text: Mix the plain yogurt starter into the cooled milk mixture until well combined.
Pour the mixture into small jars.
Place all the jars into an incubator and let them sit for 8 to 12 hours.
steps.suggested_detail: electric yogurt maker or warm oven held at 110°F (43°C)

steps.text: Chill the jars in the refrigerator (or freezer) before serving.

notes: Corrected dictation error '10 in yogurt container' to a small single cup of plain Dannon yogurt based on family answer.
Added missing step to let milk cool before adding yogurt starter, confirmed by family answer.
Added incubator details (electric yogurt maker or warm oven at 110°F/43°C) from accepted suggestion.
